themes.name: Agentic AI in research
themes.description: Focuses on AI agents that can autonomously perform research tasks, analyze data, and generate insights without constant human intervention.

themes.name: AI coding assistants
themes.description: Covers AI tools that assist developers in writing, debugging, and optimizing code, as well as exploring new coding paradigms.

themes.name: AI research tools
themes.description: Highlights platforms and applications specifically designed to aid researchers in various aspects of their work, from data analysis to literature review.

themes.name: AI customer insights
themes.description: Explores how AI is used to gather, analyze, and understand customer behavior, preferences, and feedback to drive product and service improvements.

themes.name: AI summarization
themes.description: Focuses on AI applications that condense large amounts of text, data, or conversations into concise summaries, making information more digestible.

themes.name: AI research tools comparison
themes.description: Involves articles that compare the efficacy, features, and performance of different AI tools used for research purposes.

themes.name: AI workforce impact
themes.description: Examines the effects of AI on employment, job roles, skills requirements, and the overall labor market, particularly concerning research and design professions.

themes.name: Synthetic users
themes.description: Discusses AI-generated content, images, videos, or personas that mimic human creation or interaction, and the implications for authenticity and trust.

themes.name: AI research platform
themes.description: Details dedicated platforms and ecosystems built to support and accelerate various forms of AI-driven research and development.

themes.name: AI for design & research
themes.description: Covers the application of AI tools and techniques specifically within the fields of user experience (UX) design and user research processes.

note: Themes identified by analyzing articles from curated sources, Google News, HackerNews, and DEV.to this month.
